bib.title: Orca: Progressive Learning from Complex Explanation Traces of GPT-4

question: Can a 13B model learn the reasoning process, not just the style, of GPT-4 and ChatGPT by training on large-scale, diverse, explanation-augmented imitation data, and how much of the gap does it close under a more rigorous evaluation?
hypothesis: Richer imitation signals (system-prompted explanation traces), more and more diverse tasks, and a ChatGPT intermediate teacher before GPT-4 let a small model close much of the reasoning gap that style imitation leaves open.
contributions: Explanation tuning: augment query-response pairs with detailed GPT-4 responses elicited by system instructions
Scaling tasks and instructions: sample from FLAN-v2; 5M ChatGPT responses, 1M of them also with GPT-4 responses
Evaluation: GPT-4 auto-eval on Vicuna, WizardLM, Awesome prompts; AGIEval; BBH; TruthfulQA; ToxiGen; case studies

method.summary: LLaMA-13B is fine-tuned in two stages on (system message, user query, teacher response) triples sampled from FLAN-v2: first 5M ChatGPT responses (FLAN-5M), then 1M GPT-4 responses (FLAN-1M), with 16 hand-written system messages eliciting step-by-step explanations. Evaluated zero-shot against Vicuna-13B, ChatGPT and GPT-4 on open-ended GPT-4-judged sets, AGIEval, BBH, TruthfulQA-MC and ToxiGen.
method.task: instruction tuning / explanation-trace distillation from closed-box LFMs

datasets.name: FLAN-5M (FLAN-v2 queries with ChatGPT responses)
datasets.source: Flan 2022 collection: CoT 150K (all), NiV2 440K (300 per task, stratified), Flan2021 2.5M, T0 2M (Algorithm 1 task-uniform sampling); Dialogue skipped; T0 excludes Big-Bench
datasets.preprocessing: each query paired with one of 16 system messages; only zero-shot queries

datasets.name: FLAN-1M (random subset of FLAN-5M with GPT-4 responses)
AGIEval (English MCQ)
datasets.preprocessing: first capital character of response compared with gold id

datasets.name: TruthfulQA-MC
datasets.preprocessing: questions with <4 choices removed; 4 choices sampled

other.note: intermediate teacher assistant; also baseline and GPT-4 judge reference

training.objective: next-token cross-entropy on teacher-generated tokens only (loss masked on system message and instruction)
training.epochs: 4 on FLAN-5M, then the same number (4) on FLAN-1M
training.wall_clock: 160 hours on FLAN-5M, 40 hours on FLAN-1M; data collection 2 weeks (ChatGPT) and 3 weeks (GPT-4)

other.packing: examples shuffled and grouped to at most 2048 tokens, padded
other.teacher_api_pricing: ChatGPT $0.002 per 1K tokens; GPT-4 8K $0.03 prompt / $0.06 completion per 1K

inference.decoding: sampling at temperature 0.7 for Orca in experiments; greedy decoding for the case studies
inference.prompting: zero-shot, no exemplars, no CoT; empty system message (Id 1) by default; MCQ prompt from AGIEval ending 'Among 0 through 3, the answer is'; only first capital character parsed

metrics.name: GPT-4 rated relative quality
metrics.definition: GPT-4 scores both answers 1-10 with the Vicuna template; candidate total score as a percent of reference total; reference placed first

metrics.name: AGIEval / BBH accuracy
metrics.definition: exact match of first capital character against gold answer id

metrics.name: HateBERT toxicity probability
metrics.definition: toxicity probability of continuation of ToxiGen prompts

eval.protocol: single run; no seeds or significance tests stated; ChatGPT/GPT-4/TD-003 AGIEval numbers copied from the AGIEval paper

availability.weights: planned: diff of weights at https://aka.ms/orca-lm, pending legal review

prompts.text: You are an AI assistant. User will you give you a task. Your goal is to complete the task as faithfully as you can. While performing the task think step-by-step and justify your steps.

We would like to request your feedback on the performance of two AI assistants in response to the user question displayed above. Please rate the helpfulness, relevance, accuracy, level of details of their responses.

evidence.quote: It took 160 hours to train Orca on FLAN-5M (ChatGPT augmentations) for 4 epochs

results.claim: Orca-13B retains 95% of ChatGPT quality and 85% of GPT-4 quality on open-ended generation as judged by GPT-4
results.setup: Average over Vicuna, Awesome and WizardLM prompts, GPT-4 judge, reference first, Orca vs ChatGPT
results.note: Vicuna-13B scores 85.2 vs ChatGPT in the same setup
results.quote: Orca retains 95% of ChatGPT quality and 85% of GPT-4 quality aggregated across all datasets as assessed by GPT-4.

results.claim: On AGIEval English MCQ zero-shot, Orca averages 41.7 vs Vicuna 29.3 (+42%) and retains 88% of ChatGPT
results.setup: Zero-shot, no CoT, 8 English MCQ tasks, Orca with empty system message
results.quote: Overall, Orca performs at par with Text-da-vinci-003; retaining 88% of ChatGPT quality;
results.table: Table 8, row Average, column Orca-13B (ChatGPT 47.2, GPT-4 62)

results.claim: On Big-Bench Hard zero-shot MCQ, Orca matches ChatGPT on average (49.7 vs 48.9) and more than doubles Vicuna
results.setup: Zero-shot, no exemplars, no CoT, 23 BBH task variants
results.note: Authors flag possible BBH contamination in ChatGPT/GPT-4
results.table: Table 11, row Average, column Orca-13B (ChatGPT 48.9, GPT-4 67.4, Vicuna 23.3)

results.claim: Training first on 5M ChatGPT data then 1M GPT-4 data beats GPT-4-only (1M) by 4.5 points on AGIEval
results.metric: AGIEval average gain from ChatGPT teacher assistance
results.setup: Orca vs Orca trained on FLAN-1M only, AGIEval zero-shot
results.quote: significantly improves the model performance by 4.5 points on aggregate.

results.claim: Best system message per task leaves a 4.4 point gap to ChatGPT on AGIEval
results.setup: Best of three system messages per task, AGIEval
results.quote: Orca has a performance gap of 4.4 pts against ChatGPT

results.claim: GPT-4 judging overestimates small models: Vicuna keeps 92% of ChatGPT by GPT-4 judge but only 64% on exams and 48% on BBH
results.metric: Vicuna retention of ChatGPT quality on exams
results.setup: Vicuna-13B vs ChatGPT, AGIEval professional exams

results.claim: GPT-4 judge is biased toward the first-listed model: Vicuna scores 84.87 vs 77.1 on WizardLM prompts when placed first
results.metric: Vicuna WizardLM score when listed first
results.setup: Vicuna vs ChatGPT, GPT-4 judge, order swapped
results.note: Footnote 18 gives 84.87; Table 7 gives 77.1 with ChatGPT first
results.quote: there is a positive bias in GPT-4 evaluation towards the response of the first model in the comparison set

results.claim: Training cost: 160 hours on FLAN-5M plus 40 hours on FLAN-1M on 20 A100 80GB
results.quote: It took 160 hours to train Orca on FLAN-5M (ChatGPT augmentations) for 4 epochs, and 40 hours to continue training on FLAN-1M (GPT-4 augmentations) for the same number of epochs.

results.claim: Orca is weaker than ChatGPT on math, geometry, tables and world knowledge subsets
Orca more truthful and less toxic than Vicuna but behind ChatGPT/GPT-4 on TruthfulQA-MC (read from figures, no numbers in text)
results.setup: TruthfulQA-MC 684 questions, empty system message, 1024 max tokens, temperature 0.7

results.claim: Case study: Orca gets compound-interest doubling time wrong (5 years, using 100/rate) where ChatGPT and GPT-4 use the rule of 72 and give 3.6
results.metric: Orca answer, years to double at 20%
results.quote: It will take 5 years for the item to double in value when it is growing at a 20% annual

results.claim: Case study: Orca answers the 5-clothes drying problem as 30 hours, same as ChatGPT and GPT-4 (the commonsense trap from Yejin Choi's talk)
results.metric: Orca answer, hours to dry 30 clothes
results.quote: So, it would take 30 hours to dry 30 clothes completely.

results.claim: Case study: Orca gives a wrong spatial-reasoning answer (says A is right of P) and a wrong jug-measuring procedure; GPT-4 is also marked wrong on the row puzzle
results.quote: So, the person to the right of P is A..

limits: Work in progress; weights not released at time of writing; no code
Optimizer, learning rate, schedule, batch size, precision, seeds not stated
Single runs, no significance tests or variance
Zero-shot only; multi-turn, ICL, few-shot and CoT prompting untested
Performance tied to tuning data distribution; weak in math, coding, geometry, tables
BBH contamination possible for GPT-4/ChatGPT; ChatGPT and GPT-4 AGIEval numbers copied from other work
GPT-4 judge has position and length bias; safety eval uses one detector (HateBERT) and TruthfulQA in MC form only
Safety attributed partly to Azure content filters in the teacher data, not isolated
Hallucination: small models poor as knowledge stores; research use only

Case studies show Orca failures: compound interest (5 years vs rule-of-72 3.6), seating-row puzzle (answers A), 12L/6L jug (pours 12L into 6L, no valid method), blink-count arithmetic error (72 years * 60 minutes per year = 4,320 minutes), and a quadratic-roots answer flagged 'Correct answer, Wrong format'

Case studies are single hand-picked prompts under greedy decoding, several taken from external blog/talk sources, with no counts of wins or losses; the authors mark GPT-4 as wrong on the spatial puzzle and Vicuna as wrong on temporal reasoning
Hallucination case (Fig 31): all models invent address, phone and email for a named professor; ChatGPT gets the field wrong (psychology), Orca invents a placeholder phone (555) 555-5555
